subject: Discovery recap — Mapping billing metrics to your usage patterns
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Thompson <avery@averytech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 15:14:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap — Mapping billing metrics to your usage patterns

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a concise cost estimate and next steps: 

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Primary integration: in-app assistant for customer help (chat + short generative replies).
- Throughput target: ~1200 user requests/day initially, expected to grow to 50k/month in 6–9 months.
- Ballpark budget: $18k–$25k/month for inference (in scope for this procurement round).
- Security: likely need Private (VPC) deployment if we move past POC.

Clarification items that impact cost estimates (can you confirm?):
1) Average request size: you mentioned ~600 characters per user prompt and ~1,200 characters on the model response. Is that fair? (Or please attach a few anonymized sample prompts.)
2) Are you tracking messages as distinct "requests" for the billing model (i.e., each user interaction counts as one request regardless of length)?
3) Do you care about token vs character pricing? Your procurement note referenced $/1M tokens — is that the unit you'd prefer to target, or would you like us to map to $/1M characters instead?

Quick note on caching and billed tokens: our hosted billing is per billed token (input + output) after any prefix/KV cache hits. If a prompt or prefix is served entirely from an effective prefix cache, the billed tokens for that request can be substantially lower — but that depends on your prompt structure. We can run a small sample against our cache simulator if you share real prompts.

Next steps I propose:
- You share 30–50 representative prompts and expected reply sizes (we'll anonymize and run them through our estimator).
- We produce: 1) a per-model estimate in $/1M tokens and equivalent $/1M characters, 2) recommended caching settings and expected savings, and 3) a POC plan (timeline + success metrics).

If that sounds good I can loop in engineering for a quick POC scoping call next week.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments referenced: redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (one-pager), map_tokens_vs_chars.xlsx (conversion examples)

From: Avery Thompson <avery@averytech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Mapping billing metrics to your usage patterns

Rishi —

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers below and I'll attach a sample export later today.

1) Prompt/response sizes: 600 characters in, ~1,200 characters out was our rough average — we'll send a CSV with 100 examples.
2) We currently count "requests" as user turns in our product analytics (so each interaction is one request). We're not yet tracking tokens.
3) Procurement referenced $/1M tokens because our finance team is seeing that as the industry standard. If you can map to characters that would be helpful for our internal model.

Caching question: how does Redwood treat repeated prompts? For us, ~30% of prompts are template-based (identical system prompt + variable slot values), so if Redwood can cache templates and only bill for the variable portion that would be a big cost saver.

Budget: we have approval to explore POC up to $22k/month equivalent run-rate. If your estimates look like they'd require >$30k/month at target scale we'll need to re-scope features.

I'll attach the CSV and a few example transcripts in a follow-up email this afternoon.

—Avery
Director of Product | AveryTech

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Thompson <avery@averytech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Mapping billing metrics to your usage patterns

Avery —

Appreciate the quick replies and the budget band. Monica (solutions) and Priyom (pricing) are on this thread to help with the estimator and POC plan. 

A few operational notes based on your CSV (received):
- Conversion: rough rule-of-thumb is ~4 characters ~= 1 token for English, but it varies. We ran a quick sample and your dataset averages 420 tokens per combined in+out for the typical interaction you shared.
- Billing: Redwood bills based on billed tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens minus any tokens served from an effective prefix/KV cache. That means: if a 200-token system prompt is fully cached, and the variable user content is 50 tokens, then billed tokens are primarily the variable + output. Caching works best when you can identify stable prefixes (system instructions, canned context).
- Requests vs tokens: Requests are counted for rate-limiting and request billed units (for certain enterprise plans), but per-token billing is the dominant cost driver for generative workloads.

Preliminary estimate (based on 50k monthly requests at current averages):
- Avg billed tokens/request: 420 tokens (no cache baseline)
- Monthly billed tokens: 50,000 * 420 = 21,000,000 tokens
- Target pricing target: you mentioned finance wants $/1M tokens. At $X per 1M tokens we can compute run-rate. For a quick ballpark, if we price at $25 per 1M tokens: 21 * $25 = $525/month? (note: that's incorrect math — we should compute properly.)

Priyom, can you take the numbers above and produce two clean scenarios for Avery: (A) minimal caching (5% savings), (B) aggressive prefix caching (40% savings). Include $/1M token mapping and equivalent $/1M characters so their finance team can map to existing models. Also call out where request-level billing or rate-limits would change the outcome.

Avery — once Priyom posts the scenarios we can schedule a 30-min POC scoping session. Thanks.

Best,
Rishi

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Thompson <avery@averytech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Mapping billing metrics to your usage patterns

Hi Avery —

I pulled together two concise scenarios based on the data Rishi shared and your CSV. See the highlights below; I attached a simple workbook (map_tokens_vs_chars.xlsx) in the original thread.

Scenario A — conservative caching (5% savings)
- Projected monthly requests: 50,000
- Avg billed tokens/request (baseline): 420 tokens
- Effective billed tokens after 5% cache savings: 399 tokens/request
- Monthly billed tokens: 50,000 * 399 = 19,950,000 tokens
- Cost at $25 / 1M tokens: 19.95 * $25 = $498.75k/year (~$41.5k/month)
- Equivalent characters: we used 4 chars/token => ~79.8M characters/month => $ per 1M chars = (cost / 79.8) => see workbook.

Scenario B — aggressive prefix caching (40% savings on cached portion)
- Effective billed tokens/request after caching: 252 tokens/request (40% drop on the cached portion, net 40% on overall in+out in our sample)
- Monthly billed tokens: 50,000 * 252 = 12,600,000 tokens
- Cost at $25 / 1M tokens: 12.6 * $25 = $315k/year (~$26.25k/month)

Notes and clarifications:
- The $25 / 1M tokens example is a placeholder for scenario illustration. Redwood has tiered pricing and volume discounts; we can target a committed $/1M token that brings your run-rate within the $22k/month approval if we structure a reserved capacity commitment or POC credits.
- Billed tokens include both input + output after caching reductions. If you adopt prefix templates and send only variables at runtime (or use server-side template resolution), you can push savings towards scenario B.
- Requests and rate limits: If you expect spikes, Dedicated capacity with burst options reduces request throttling and can change optimal batch/caching settings. That does add a fixed seat/reserved cost component.

Next steps I recommend:
1) We run a 2-week POC on Redwood hosted with the sample prompts (we'll simulate caching and report expected billed tokens).
2) If the POC shows run-rate at or below ~$22k/month equivalent we can move to a 6–12 month reserved proposal to lock pricing.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Priyom Das
Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference

On attachments: redwood-pricing-summary.pdf, map_tokens_vs_chars.xlsx, sample_prompt_set.json
